statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds. If there is no integer v such that v lies on at least one diagonal of nums and v is prime, then r = 0. Otherwise, r is prime, r lies on at least one diagonal of nums, and for every v that lies on at least one diagonal of nums, if v is prime then v <= r. Here v lies on at least one diagonal of nums iff there exists i with 0 <= i < n and (nums[i][i] = v or nums[i][n - 1 - i] = v); and v is prime iff v > 1 and there is no integer d with 2 <= d < v such that d divides v.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies: 1 <= n <= 300; for every i with 0 <= i < n, len(nums[i]) = n; and for every i, j with 0 <= i < n and 0 <= j < n, 1 <= nums[i][j] <= 4000000.
